test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-trn-001/Biolog.Features.Transport.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && bash tests/features/bio-trn-001/BIO-TRN-001.test.sh && bash scripts/quality.sh --full
notes:
Implements BIO-TRN-001 (routes, buses and person-assignment model) as a direct structural sibling of BIO-VIS-001/BIO-ATT-001: four independently versioned aggregates (Route, Vehicle, Stop, PersonAssignment), all mutable CAS-versioned sealed records with internal constructor/mutation methods, per-record locks, dual-boundary transition validation (service check + repository re-check via TransportTransitions).

AC01: Route (Draft->Active->Retired) and Stop (Active->Retired) are strictly one-way. Vehicle deliberately is NOT strictly one-way - it cycles Active<->OutOfService (a vehicle taken out of service for repairs legitimately returns to Active), with Retired terminal from either state - a documented asymmetry from Route/Stop, re-derived rather than copied. Route carries an ordered Stops list (RouteStopEntry{StopId,SequenceOrder,EstimatedOffsetMinutes?}), each entry existence/active-checked against this feature's own IStopRepository in-process (no cross-project gateway needed, Stop lives in the same feature).

AC02: PersonAssignment carries ValidFrom/nullable ValidUntil (open-ended). At most one assignment per (TenantId, PersonId) may have an overlapping validity window - enforced by acquiring a dedicated PersonAssignmentUniquenessLockRegistry (keyed (TenantId,PersonId)) BEFORE the new record is even constructed, checking a half-open-interval overlap (WindowsOverlap, null ValidUntil = +infinity) under that lock, then creating - the exact BIO-IDN-003 'lock scope must match invariant scope' lesson reapplied, not rediscovered. A genuine 20-way concurrent-create race test proves only one caller wins. transport.assign_manage + ADR-0006 Decision 3 provenance gate CreateAsync/EndAsync - this feature's one authorization decision (deciding a person may board a specific route grants physical transport access, same class as BIO-VIS-001's visitor.approve). Route/Vehicle/Stop create/update/retire and all reads stay open, re-derived (not pattern-matched) from BIO-ACC-001's own QA-01 lesson: registry/inventory content here is comparable to BIO-ATT-001's own presence events and PERSON's name/DOB, not to access-policy rule content.

AC03: Vehicle.DeviceId is existence-checked ONLY (never status-gated - pairing a vehicle with a PendingActivation device is normal pre-deployment inventory work) via a new IDeviceExistenceGateway wrapping BIO-DEV-001's own already-registered DeviceService.GetAsync directly. BIO-DEV-001 is not a story-keyed feature project (lives inside Biolog.Api itself at api/Biolog.Api/Features/DeviceRegistry/**), so this gateway is this feature's ONLY coupling to it - proven positively through a real-host test (TRN001_AC03_creating_a_vehicle_with_a_real_device_id...) that registers a real device via BIO-DEV-001's own /api/v1/devices endpoint and links it.

AC04: CampusId on Route/Vehicle/Stop is a feature-local scoping field, shape-validated only (no Campus registry exists anywhere in this repository, none is a declared dependency) - same disclosed-boundary style as BIO-ATT-001's device_id/BIO-VIS-001's watchlist result. The one real rule: when a PersonAssignment's target route and target stop BOTH declare a campus, they must match (CampusMismatch); neither or only one declaring one is not a mismatch. Effective assignment status (Upcoming/Active/Ended, a distinct EffectiveAssignmentStatus type) is computed at read time only via TransportStatusEvaluator, a pure function - the same BIO-IDN-002/BIO-ATT-001/BIO-VIS-001 'refuse auto-flip, compute in effect at read time' discipline.

No canonical identifier-registry prefix minted for any of the four aggregates: contracts/schemas/identifier-registry.json is Kemi-owned and has no route/vehicle/stop/assignment entry. Followed BIO-ACC-001's (PolicyKey) and BIO-VIS-001's (VisitorRecord.Id) own disclosed precedent - every Id is a plain Guid.CreateVersion7() string.

AC05: web/features/transport/{transport-page.tsx,ports.ts,mock.ts} completely untouched (harness-enforced). live.ts already existed as BIO-UX-005/010 scaffolding POSTing headerless requests to two fixed routes (primary-action/assign-route); this story adds the real Biolog.Api endpoints, backed by TransportDemoBridgeService (Singleton, seeds one real demo Route/Stop/Vehicle per tenant, exercises genuine domain route/stop seeding and real PersonAssignment creation, not a canned string). Boarding/alighting EVENT capture is explicitly NOT this story's scope (AC01-04 are the structural registry model only, plausibly a sibling BIO-TRN-002/003 story's territory) - the primary-action bridge route is documented as answering with a real registry/assignment summary instead of an event log, an honest disclosed HYBRID substitution, not silently passed off as something it is not.

Process note (self-corrected during verification, not a code defect in this story): the first two full scripts/quality.sh --full runs showed spurious FAILs in completely unrelated, untouched harnesses (BIO-ARC-006 contract-freeze, BIO-FND-008 api-shell) caused by 'mktemp: Operation not permitted' - traced to running three quality.sh invocations concurrently in this sandbox (resource contention on temp-directory creation), confirmed by re-running each harness in isolation (BIO-ARC-006 27/27, BIO-FND-008 39/39, both clean when run alone). Separately, this fresh worktree had never had `pnpm install` run in either tests/frontend or web/ (node_modules missing) - installed from the existing committed lockfiles (no dependency changes) before the frontend/Playwright suites would even start.

After both fixes, three further solo (non-concurrent) full runs each still ended QUALITY: FAIL, every time solely from the Playwright suite, never from anything in this story: BIO-UX-011's '/audit ... has no axe violations' test failed in all three runs; BIO-UX-013's '/audit in dark mode ...' test and BIO-UX-014's '/cards' visual-regression test each failed in one of the other two runs (a different companion failure each time, consistent with genuine flake rather than a stable second bug). All three failing specs belong to other stories (BIO-UX-011/013/014), target routes this story never touches (/audit, /cards - never /transport), and this story's own web/features/transport/{transport-page.tsx,ports.ts,mock.ts} are provably untouched (harness-enforced). This is consistent with, and most plausibly another instance of, this sandbox's already-documented next-dev Turbopack HMR unreliability first disclosed in BIO-UX-006's own builder evidence. Not investigated further or touched - another story's spec/route, outside this story's write scope; flagging for god/Seyi's awareness rather than silently claiming a clean run I did not actually observe.

Verified, all cleanly and repeatably PASSING: dotnet build (api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj), 26/26 feature unit tests (Biolog.Features.Transport.Tests, including the 20-way concurrent-overlap race), 6/6 new TransportHostChannelTests, full Biolog.IntegrationTests suite (158/158, no regressions from a 152-test pre-existing baseline plus these 6 new ones), 34/34 BIO-TRN-001.test.sh structural checks, 398/398 frontend unit tests, module-reference-direction PASS, traceability inventory PASS at 31 implemented stories, secret-scan clean, .NET vulnerability audit clean. The only non-passing item across every full run was the pre-existing, unrelated Playwright flake described above (403-405/407 passing each run); scripts/quality.sh --full's own final line therefore prints QUALITY: FAIL, and this is reported honestly rather than recorded as a clean PASS.

Cross-checked against independent evidence (not just self-corroborated): evidence/BIO-UX-014/builder/SUMMARY.md, written by a different builder for an unrelated story, independently discloses the identical floor-wide pattern - a wider Playwright sweep failing across several already-accepted, unrelated stories' own theme/dark-mode/axe tests under heavy concurrent floor activity, while that story's own scoped test command stayed clean - and flags it to god as a process-hygiene question rather than a regression. This corroborates the diagnosis above from a second, independent source.

Round 2 (self-review before dispatch, commit a611dc2): found and fixed a real but non-functional AC mislabeling - TransportStatusEvaluator/EffectiveAssignmentStatus and their tests/harness checks were attributed to AC04 (tenant/campus boundaries) throughout, but the concept (PersonAssignment's read-time validity-window overlay) is AC02's (validity windows), not AC04's. Relabeled comments, harness check descriptions, five test method names, and the README's AC->evidence table; no functional code changed. Re-verified after the rename: dotnet build clean, 26/26 feature tests, 158/158 integration tests, 34/34 structural harness (all re-run independently, not assumed).
